t1.goal: Download the nginx image with docker pull nginx and confirm it appears in docker images.
steps: Open the Docker CLI.
Type: docker pull nginx
Type: docker images
Check nginx is listed in the REPOSITORY column.
t1.done_when: At least one image is present in the Docker engine's image list.
t1.ask_ai: What is the difference between an image and a container?

t2.goal: Start a detached container named web from the nginx image so it is running in the background.
steps: Open the Docker CLI.
Type: docker run -d --name web nginx
Type: docker ps and check web is listed with status Up.
t2.done_when: A container named web exists with status running.
t2.ask_ai: What does -d change, and what happens to my terminal without it?

t3.goal: Run the hello-world image as a container named hello, let it exit, and find it again with docker ps -a.
steps: Open the Docker CLI.
Type: docker run --name hello hello-world
Type: docker ps - hello is not there because it is not running.
Type: docker ps -a and check hello shows as Exited (0).
t3.done_when: At least one container exists with status exited.
t3.ask_ai: Why does an exited container still block its name from being reused?

t4.goal: Read the output of the web container with docker logs web.
steps: Open the Docker CLI.
Type: docker logs web
Read the nginx startup lines it prints.
t4.done_when: You have run a docker logs command.
t4.ask_ai: Where do container logs come from - what does the app have to write to?

t5.goal: Remove the exited hello container with docker rm hello so it no longer exists.
steps: Open the Docker CLI.
Type: docker rm hello
Type: docker ps -a and check hello is gone (web is still there).
t5.done_when: You have run a docker rm command and no container named hello exists any more.
t5.ask_ai: When would I use docker rm -f, and what is the risk?

t1.goal: Build a topology of two PCs connected to one switch in the Network Simulator studio.
steps: Open the Network Simulator.
Drag one switch and two PCs onto the canvas.
Connect each PC to a different port on the switch with a cable.
Check both links show as up.
t1.done_when: You press 'I have done this' once two PCs are cabled to one switch and the links are up.
t1.ask_ai: What does a switch do with a frame when it does not yet know where the destination MAC lives?

t2.goal: Give the PCs 192.168.10.10/24 and 192.168.10.11/24 and ping one from the other successfully.
steps: Open the Network Simulator and select the first PC; set its IP to 192.168.10.10 with mask 255.255.255.0 (/24).
Set the second PC to 192.168.10.11 with mask 255.255.255.0.
From the first PC, ping 192.168.10.11.
Open the packet trace and find the ARP request and ARP reply before the ping replies.
t2.done_when: You press 'I have done this' once the ping between the two /24 hosts succeeds and you have seen the ARP exchange.
t2.ask_ai: Why does the first ping need an ARP exchange, and why does the second ping not?

t3.goal: Open one ping packet in the trace and read its frame, IP packet and ICMP payload layer by layer.
steps: Open the Network Simulator and ping between the two PCs again.
Open the packet trace and expand one hop.
Read the Ethernet frame (source and destination MAC), the IP packet (source and destination IP, TTL) and the ICMP payload (echo request or reply).
t3.done_when: You press 'I have done this' once you have expanded a packet and identified its frame, packet and ICMP layers.
t3.ask_ai: Which fields change at each hop and which stay the same end to end?

t4.goal: Change one host to a /25 mask, move the other to 192.168.10.200/24, ping, and explain why it fails from the /25 side.
steps: Open the Network Simulator and change the first PC's mask to 255.255.255.128 (/25), keeping 192.168.10.10.
Change the second PC's address to 192.168.10.200/24.
Ping 192.168.10.200 from the /25 host and watch the trace: it looks for a gateway because .200 is outside 192.168.10.0 - 192.168.10.127.
Put the masks back to /24 and confirm the ping works again.
t4.done_when: You press 'I have done this' once you have reproduced the mask-mismatch failure and can explain which host thinks the other is off-net.
t4.ask_ai: Why is a subnet mask mismatch not symmetrical between the two hosts?

t5.goal: Work out by hand the network, broadcast and host range for 10.20.30.45/26, then check it in the simulator.
steps: On paper, compute the block size: 256 - 192 = 64, so the networks are .0, .64, .128 and .192.
Write down the network address, broadcast address and usable host range for 10.20.30.45 (you should get 10.20.30.0, 10.20.30.63 and .1 - .62).
Open the Network Simulator, give a host 10.20.30.45/26 and confirm the simulator's network and broadcast match yours.
Repeat the paper calculation for two more addresses of your choice.
t5.done_when: You press 'I have done this' once your hand calculation for the /26 matches what the simulator shows.
t5.ask_ai: How do I quickly find the block size for any mask like /27 or /28?

t3.goal: Add a link with a real href, for example Self Study, to your page.

t4.goal: Add an element that has an alt attribute describing the image.

Type:

t1.goal: Run makemigrations and migrate so auth_user and every other table exist and nothing is unapplied.
steps: Open the Django console.
Type: python manage.py makemigrations
Type: python manage.py migrate
Check the Project pane says nothing is unapplied.
t1.ask_ai: Which built-in Django apps create tables when I run migrate for the first time?

t2.goal: Create a superuser named admin with python manage.py createsuperuser --username admin --email admin@example.com.
steps: Open the Django console.
Type: python manage.py createsuperuser --username admin --email admin@example.com
Enter a password when asked.
Check the Project pane lists the superuser.
t2.done_when: Django has at least one superuser.
t2.ask_ai: Why does createsuperuser fail with no such table: auth_user before migrate?

t3.goal: Register your models with the admin using admin.site.register in shop/admin.py.
steps: In the Files tool, open shop/admin.py.
Add: from django.contrib import admin and from .models import Category, Product
Add: admin.site.register(Category) and admin.site.register(Product), then save.
t3.ask_ai: What does registering a model with the admin give me for free?

t4.goal: Give a model in shop/models.py a __str__(self) method that returns its name.
steps: In the Files tool, open shop/models.py.
Inside class Product add: def __str__(self): with body return self.name (indented correctly).
Save the file.
t4.ask_ai: Where else, besides the admin, does __str__ make my models easier to read?

t5.goal: Find your superuser in the database with python manage.py dbshell and SELECT username, is_superuser FROM auth_user;.
steps: Open the Django console.
Type: python manage.py dbshell
Type: SELECT username, email, is_superuser FROM auth_user;
Check the admin row has is_superuser set to 1.
t5.done_when: You have run dbshell or a SELECT ... auth_user query.
t5.ask_ai: Why is the password column in auth_user not the password I typed?
